reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: An admission decision is always a human decision. The platform already enforces this structurally rather than by policy: internshipStateMachine.ts:155 and :170 list only the reviewer actor on every edge into approved, rejected and waitlisted, and canTransition at :264-279 deliberately takes no override, force or isAdmin parameter, so there is no argument an agent could pass to make itself a reviewer. The agent's ceiling is therefore autonomy:R2, answering questions about decisions already recorded. It may prepare a decision packet under admissions.reviewer_decision_packet_assembly; it may never make, advance or self-approve a decision at any autonomy level, including autonomy:R9.

Detection is read-only aggregate work that changes nothing, so autonomy:R7 is reachable for the 'report an anomaly' action class. The expected ranges stay human-set, because a detector that tunes its own thresholds can tune away the alert it does not want to raise.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Drafting carries no PII and is reversible, but activating an entry changes what the organisation tells every subsequent applicant, which makes activation a human decision. Supervised drafting (autonomy:R6) is the ceiling, and the active flag stays a human write.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Auditing route-to-section coverage reads only code and changes nothing, so autonomy:R7 is reachable. Adding a PATH_SECTION row changes who can reach applicant data, so that write is always a human decision reviewed by someone who can say which section a surface belongs to.

Placing a call reaches an applicant's phone, which is an irreversible external side effect on a person. The existing design keeps it applicant-initiated, and that is the property to preserve: an agent may prepare the prompt and read the outcome, so its ceiling is stateful sandbox work (autonomy:R4). Dialling stays with the applicant's own request, never with the agent's judgement that a call would be useful.

This is the capability that most tempts a system into deciding, so its ceiling is set by what it must never become. It reads an applicant's resume, phone number and interview transcript and produces text a reviewer leans on. Shadow mode against decisions a reviewer already made (autonomy:R5) is the highest honest level: it proves the assessment is sound without the assessment ever carrying authority. It must never reach autonomy:R7, because an automated assessment that a reviewer rubber-stamps is an automated decision wearing a recommendation's clothes.

This is a read-only reconstruction that changes nothing, which argues for a high ceiling. It stops at a supervised production pilot (autonomy:R6) rather than autonomy:R7 for one reason: the trail is the evidence base for an admissions outcome, and an agent that reads it unattended should be doing so under a named human's supervision until the free-text reason column is proven not to carry applicant PII that a summary could re-expose.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This capability reads code and configuration, never applicant data, which is why its own pii_exposure is none. Producing the matrix is an authorizable action class at autonomy:R7. Acting on it, by narrowing a grant or dropping a column, is a human decision with a migration behind it, which is why human_decision is true.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Drafting is reversible; sending is not. Sending requires the default-denied live_email capability, so the ceiling is multi-step drafting in sandbox (autonomy:R4). It is marked human_decision because the act that matters, publication to a named applicant, is a human act, and because an unreviewed draft pipeline is indistinguishable in effect from an automated send.

Reading the queue means reading the applicant's name, email and phone from the joined enrollment, and mgmtRoles.ts:22-27 records that this is deliberately a wider grant than curriculum access. Until Taiwo has a surface on which to approve that read and a field-level minimisation rule exists, the ceiling is stateful sandbox work on fixtures (autonomy:R4). Reaching production reads is a separate approval, not an extension of this one.

Booking writes into a named colleague's calendar and schedules a real person's time, which is an external side effect on two people at once. Offering slots and simulating the booking in sandbox (autonomy:R4) is the ceiling, and the booking itself stays with the prospect's own click on the live public route.

Identifying and listing is safe, but this capability names individual students as at-risk, which is a judgement that reaches them if it is acted on. A supervised production pilot (autonomy:R6) is the ceiling, and the nudge itself belongs to whichever capability holds the contact channel, never to this one.
Managing a queue is an internal bookkeeping action class that may reach autonomy:R7. Placing the call is a separate capability with a separate and much lower ceiling, and this one must never dial.

An end-of-cohort aggregate retrospective changes nothing and can be produced without naming anyone, so autonomy:R7 is reachable. Its one discipline is that it must never infer a drop reason, because a fabricated reason propagates into curriculum decisions and compounds.

Detecting and recording a request is reversible internal bookkeeping, so autonomy:R7 is reachable for that action class. Fulfilling the request is explicitly a different capability, because the fulfilment channels (email, SMS, voice) are the ones that reach a person.

A wrong merge joins two different people's conversations into one record, which is a data-protection failure that re-running cannot cleanly undo. A supervised production pilot (autonomy:R6) is the ceiling until a verified no-false-merge rate exists.

This capability writes a persistent characterisation of a named person that later prompts read back, and MEMORY_MAP.md:12 records no human-approval path for personality_notes. Until an approval path exists it stops at a supervised production pilot (autonomy:R6) rather than reaching the unattended automation of autonomy:R7.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Deciding that a human's responsibility moves to a machine is a decision about a person's job, and it is not one an agent may make or even recommend unprompted. The agent may assemble the map from evidence (autonomy:R2); every transition on it is approved by Taiwo and by Ali.

Producing an aggregate internal report is exactly the kind of explicitly authorizable action class autonomy:R7 is for, and the brief already describes it as something that generates daily once the columns and thresholds are given. Distribution by mail requires the default-denied live_email capability, so the agent renders and an approved mail path or a human sends. The thresholds stay Taiwo's, because a self-set escalation threshold is a self-granted exemption.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Telling a person they were rejected is the single least reversible thing in this domain. Sending it requires the default-denied live_email capability (executionPolicy.ts:27), so the agent may render and preview in sandbox (autonomy:R4) and nothing more. It is marked human_decision because the decision the message conveys is a human decision and the send is its irrevocable publication.

A read-only health rollup over internal telemetry carries no applicant exposure and changes nothing, so autonomy:R7 is reachable. It must never gain the ability to disable or re-enable a component it reports on, because a reporter that can silence its own findings is not a reporter.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Which responsibilities belong to which AI employee is a governance decision about accountability, and an agent that could set its own scope could extend it. The agent may lay out the conflict with citations (autonomy:R2); the boundary is Ali's to draw.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Raising a flag is not deciding, so sandbox multi-step work (autonomy:R4) is reachable. It is marked human_decision because the flag's only consequence is a human judgement about a person's eligibility, and AI_INTERNSHIP_DISCOVERY.md:175-186 explicitly forbids the flag ever becoming an automatic rejection. The ceiling therefore stops well below automation: an automated eligibility conclusion is an automated admission decision.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A conversion initiative changes how Colaberry treats prospective applicants and commits other people's work, which is a strategic decision reserved for a human. The agent may propose and may shadow-evaluate against initiatives a human already ran (autonomy:R5), but it may never adopt an initiative, so it stops below the supervised production pilot and well below automation.
Flagging is additive and reversible and triggers no contact. Capped at autonomy:R7 for the 'flag a lead as enterprise' action class only; the enterprise conversation itself is human work.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A threshold is the definition of what counts as a problem, so an agent that can set its own threshold can decide what it never has to report. The agent may read thresholds and propose one with evidence; setting or changing one is always a human write. The ceiling is autonomy:R2 and this is a structural limit rather than a staged one.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: The plan half is a pure read and could sit higher, but commit writes application rows for named people and an ambiguous match resolved wrongly merges or splits a real person's record. Shadow planning against conversions a human already committed (autonomy:R5) is the ceiling. Commit stays human, which preserves the structural dry-run guarantee the service was built around.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Activation is the moment an applicant becomes a person with paid programme access, which is the advancement of an admission. It is therefore a human decision and the agent's ceiling is computing blockers against sandbox fixtures (autonomy:R4). An agent may never activate anyone, and it may never mark an onboarding requirement satisfied on an applicant's behalf.

Asking the next approved question is bounded work, but the answers are the applicant's own words in a record that feeds an admission decision, and the interview_complete transition it can trigger moves the application forward. Multi-step sandbox work (autonomy:R4) is the ceiling until Taiwo has approved what an agent may ask and store. It may never evaluate an answer as good or bad, which would be assessing, nor transition past interview_complete.

The transcript is the single richest piece of unstructured applicant PII in the system and the extraction feeds an admission decision. Shadow mode against applicant-confirmed answers (autonomy:R5) is the ceiling: it measures extraction fidelity against the person's own confirmation, which is the only correct reference. It must never reach a level at which an extracted answer is stored as confirmed, because internshipTranscriptExtraction.ts:11-13 makes applicant confirmation the control.

The knowledge base is what the assistant quotes to applicants, so an unreviewed auto-update propagates straight into applicant-facing claims. Drafting and flagging may reach autonomy:R6 under supervision; activating a changed entry stays a human step, which is why this does not reach autonomy:R7.

Ingest is already deterministic and idempotent by design, which is what makes a high ceiling arguable. It stops at a supervised production pilot (autonomy:R6) because a wrong tier-2 match writes one person's enquiry onto another person's record, and because raw_lead_payloads holds whole untrusted bodies that no field-level restriction currently fences off.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Creating an identity that can read applicant data is an access grant, and an agent that can grant access can grant itself access. The agent's ceiling is autonomy:R2: report the blocker, name the three gates and name the approver. The grant is Ali's write and the verification is an observed human login.

Answering from approved knowledge is autonomy:R2 work by definition, and the live surface already runs unattended. The ceiling is autonomy:R7 for the narrow action class 'reply from approved admissions knowledge'. It may never state an admission outcome, an eligibility conclusion or a price absent from approved knowledge, and it may never advance an application state.

An aggregate internal revenue report changes nothing and names nobody, so autonomy:R7 is reachable for the 'produce the monthly report' action class. The price table stays a human input, because a revenue figure computed from a price the agent inferred is a fabricated revenue figure.

An offer document is a quasi-contractual artifact carrying a named person's legal name and a start date. Generating one in production is a commitment the organisation makes, so the agent's ceiling is sandbox generation against fixtures (autonomy:R4). Production generation and delivery stay with the reviewer who made the decision the document expresses.

This capability only reads and reports; it changes nothing. That makes autonomy:R7 reachable for the 'produce a compliance finding' action class. It must never acquire the power to approve an outbound contact, because a monitor that can grant its own exemptions is not a monitor.

The write is a derived tag on a record that already exists, reversible by re-running, and it touches no applicant-facing surface, so an explicitly authorized 'tag a visitor interest signal' action class at autonomy:R7 is defensible. It stops there because autonomy:R8 handoffs do not exist on this platform.

Composing an internal aggregate update is an authorizable action class at autonomy:R7. Distribution is the constrained part: delivering it by mail needs the default-denied live_email capability, so the agent renders and a human or an already-approved mail service sends.

This capability initiates contact with a person, but only inside a page the person already has open and only through a widget the person can dismiss. It never reaches an inbox or a phone. That keeps it inside an authorizable action class at autonomy:R7, conditional on a frequency cap Taiwo sets.

Counting and trending refunds is read-only aggregate work, so autonomy:R7 is reachable for producing the report. The capability is bounded on the other side by the brief itself: proposing or changing refund policy is Ali's decision, so the agent reports the pattern and never recommends the remedy.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This is the clearest expression of the domain's central rule: an agent may prepare a decision and may never make one. Shadow assembly against applications already decided (autonomy:R5) proves the packet is complete and unbiased without the packet ever carrying authority. It stops below automation because a packet produced unattended, read by a reviewer under time pressure, is functionally a decision.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Reconciling names reads only code and configuration, so autonomy:R7 is reachable for producing the report. Correcting a name changes which registry row governs a running behaviour, including its enabled flag and its tool grants, so that write is a human decision and sits outside this programme's scope entirely.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Verification is the gate that converts an applicant into a person with paid programme access, and AI_INTERNSHIP_DISCOVERY.md:118-139 records that getting it wrong grants full paid training free and forever. It is reviewer-only on the state machine edge, so the agent's ceiling is autonomy:R2, answering questions about verifications already performed. An agent may never verify a document, and an agent may never self-verify a document it generated.

Read-only aggregation with small-group suppression carries no individual exposure and changes nothing, so autonomy:R7 is reachable. It must never be allowed to drill from an aggregate down to a named person, because that would convert an aggregate_only capability into an applicant_identifiable one without a new approval.

A score is a recommendation, not an action: nothing downstream of this capability may contact anybody or change an application state. Capped at autonomy:R7 and only for the 'write an intent reading' action class, with the thresholds themselves remaining a human setting.

This report already runs unattended on a weekly cron and the snapshot write is idempotent, so autonomy:R7 reflects what is true rather than what is aspirational. It names individual students, so it must never acquire the ability to contact one of them: the at-risk list is a handoff to a human, which is a separate capability.

authority_rule.rule: A capability approved above autonomy:R2 with no granted tools is forced back down to autonomy:R2, with the reason no_tool_grants. Tool grants are the throttle.
authority_rule.note: When this binds nothing, say so in words. It means no capability in this domain has been approved above autonomy:R2 yet, not that the rule is absent or that the panel failed.

governance.disclosure: A filed request grants nothing. Status is what a named human decided, and a pending row means nobody has decided yet.

verification.disclosure: A criterion counts as passing when it is marked in `.colaberry/progress.json` in this repository. The verifier reads that file on every sync and records what it found. A story showing 0 of N is not a rejection: nothing has been claimed yet.
